newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS AND PORK BELLIES END MOSTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS AND PORK BELLIES END MOSTLY HIGHER.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures ended mostly higher after trading that way much of the day with limit gains in CBOT corn futures supporting deferred hog contracts, traders said.
Hogs closed off 0.525 cent per lb to up 0.450 with only August and December off and October up 0.200 at 72.050 cents. August was off most at 79.875 cents.
Pork bellies settled 1.075 cent a lb higher to 0.550 lower with August up most at 82.200 cents and February up 0.625 at 74.650 cents.
August hogs were pulled down by current cash hog values but October rose on an oversold condition, traders said.

Steady to possibly weak cash hog indications for Wednesday and rolling out of long positions ahead of its expiration on Thursday pressured August. October lacked follow-through technical selling and rose on short covering while December was pushed down by spreading against long positions in next year contracts following the surge in corn prices, sources said.
ADM Investor Services, LIT division of First Options and Lind-Waldock sold October late before Rand Financials and Iowa Grain bought near the close to support that month.
In hog options, ADM bought August 80 puts and commission house sold October 70 puts, pit sources said.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.57 to $79.42 per cwt.

Pork belly futures traded quietly much of the day with support generated by expectations cash belly prices were near a near-term bottom. Fresh 14-16 lb bellies held their lower end of the trading range in the cash market at $78 per cwt at midday, which prompted late mixed support in August belly futures and local short covering in February, traders said.
After the close, CME reported a net out-movement of 3.516 million lbs at out-of-town warehouses, within the range of early estimates of out 3.0 million to 3.7 million lbs.
